federal.text: A retailer may not sell covered tobacco products with the assistance of any electronic or mechanical device (such as a vending machine), except in facilities where the retailer ensures that no person younger than 21 years of age is present, or permitted to enter, at any time.
federal.note: E-cigarettes/ENDS are 'covered tobacco products' (deemed in 2016). For them the operative vending rule is 1140.14(b)(3). 1140.16(c)(2)(ii) is the parallel rule for cigarettes and smokeless tobacco. Both use the same 21+ facility test.
federal.ageVerification: Neither section has an exception for ID scanners, facial age estimation, or remote-unlock machines. The test is about the facility (no one under 21 present or allowed in at any time), not the machine. We found no FDA guidance that treats age-verifying machines as compliant in all-ages venues. Status: no exception found in the regulation text. Ask FDA CTP or counsel before relying on any vendor claim.
federal.pact: PACT Act (15 U.S.C. 375 et seq., amended in 2020 to cover ENDS) governs delivery sales and remote/mail sales: registration, age verification at delivery, and USPS mailing restrictions. In-person vending is not a delivery sale, but any online pre-order or ship-to-machine model may trigger PACT. Status: general reading, not verified for any specific business model.

states.vending: A.R.S. 36-798.02 limits tobacco-product vending machines to bars and non-public employee lounges in businesses with no minor employees. The 36-798 definition of 'tobacco products' (cigarettes, papers, cigars, smokeless, smoking tobacco) does not expressly name vapor/alternative nicotine products, so the state vending statute's reach over vapes is unclear (unverified). The federal 21+ facility rule applies either way.
states.age: 21: A.R.S. 13-3622 covers tobacco and 'alternative nicotine products'. Escalating enterprise penalties, up to a class 5/6 felony for repeat violations.
states.license: No statewide tobacco retail license found (unverified). Local licenses apply in Tucson ($300/yr) and some other cities.
states.tax: Unverified. Confirm vapor excise and transaction privilege tax (TPT) treatment with AZ Dept of Revenue.

states.vending: Tex. Health & Safety Code 161.086: vendor-assisted sales are required, and machines selling e-cigarettes are allowed only where the premises is not open to people under 21 at any time. A 161.084 warning sign is required.
states.license: Comptroller e-cigarette retailer permit required for each location.

states.vending: NRS 202.2494 allows cigarette vending machines only in areas where people under 21 may not loiter. We found no express provision for vapor-product vending (unverified). The federal 21+ facility rule applies.
states.license: Retail license for tobacco/vapor sellers via NV Dept of Taxation (verify).

states.vending: 720 ILCS 675/1: vending of e-cigarettes is allowed only in places where under-21s are barred at all times, or in alcohol establishments under direct supervision. Each machine needs its own retailer license.
states.license: State tobacco retailer license for each machine (IDOR).
states.flavor: Chicago city flavor ban on flavored liquid nicotine (O2020-3388, effective Oct 2020).
states.tax: State and Cook County/Chicago taxes on e-cigs (verify current rates).

states.vending: Colorado prohibits vending-machine sales of cigarettes, tobacco, and nicotine products. The one exception is cigarettes in age-restricted areas of licensed gaming establishments.
states.license: State tobacco/nicotine retail license (DOR Specialized Business Group).
states.flavor: Denver flavored-tobacco ban (2024 ordinance; hookah excluded). Verify the effective date.
states.tax: State nicotine products tax (Prop EE). Verify the rate.

states.vending: Bus. & Prof. Code 22960 prohibits selling tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, from vending machines. The narrow exception is on-sale alcohol premises, with the machine at least 15 ft from the entrance.
states.flavor: Statewide flavor ban (SB 793, upheld Nov 2022; AB 3218, 2025). San Diego and Los Angeles also have local flavor ordinances.
states.tax: CA excise and retail tax on e-cigs (verify).

states.vending: Public Health Law 1399-dd allows e-cig vending only in bars, private clubs, tobacco businesses, or qualifying workplaces, in plain view and directly supervised. Laundromats do not qualify.

arizonaLocal.finding: Tobacco retail license required, $300/yr per location (City Code ch.7 art. XIX; T21 Ord. 11703 broadened 'tobacco product' to nicotine products). City Code 11-93 bans tobacco vending machines in public places except liquor-licensed bars, within 10 ft of the bar and visible to staff. Whether 11-93's older definition reaches vapes is unverified. 2023 UDC smoke-shop zoning amendment.
City Code 7-09 (Tobacco Products) treats electronic smoking devices as tobacco products and generally prohibits vending/self-service except where minors have no access.
arizonaLocal.status: reported (search summary; read the code text before relying)

arizonaLocal.finding: No city tobacco retail license ordinance found in this pass.
Tempe has a Tobacco 21 ordinance (2018). Licensing and vending specifics not checked.
The AG's Tobacco Enforcement Unit runs compliance checks and publishes the state tobacco law summary.
